question.problem:
For the function $f:{R}^{2}\to R,$ defined as

$$
f(x)={e}^{xy},\,x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}],
$$

calculate ${f}^{′}(x).$

current_example.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $\boldsymbol{f}:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m$ is defined by 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14196264/assets/c0eaadc2f0732363b5aba88635942a6150dca944cb8e8a7b4cc3d26f7e0a8401.svg) 

where $f_1,f_2,\ldots,f_m$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $\boldsymbol f$ is differentiable at $\mathbf{x},$ then the total derivative of $\boldsymbol f$ at $\mathbf{x},$ denoted $\boldsymbol{f}'(\mathbf{x}),$ is given by the $m \times n$ matrix

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14196264/assets/ab208614166169548d7127bedd5c2fdd4f099aee8b87a3b3d4e045f0688dcc23.svg)

In our case, we have the following:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14196264/assets/310f21a1ea3f5af9fa443c8084cee0bb46a690fe2c387dfbcae237184f264234.svg)

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}y)=2xy, & \,\frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}y)={x}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

and $\boldsymbol{f}'$ at ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14196264/assets/062662c053f11d55d37bce15295433d8ecebe7cabd0ed4137249464e76580810.svg) is
